notes: The pack does what its README says and nothing more. Its single pass reads sessions and notes, makes one call for all notes (per_note = false), and works only on notes that sessions touched or cited, which is the scope its purpose needs; the fixture checks that an untouched note (Archive / 'Orchard ledger') stays out of the prompt. The prompt treats untrusted blocks as data. It allows only `append` changes with an empty `old`, and each change may only add `Related: [[title]]` lines under a final `## Related` section. Each link must connect two notes that a cited session's handoff connects, and its title must appear in the notes input. The prompt forbids instructions, commands or links that only tool output shows, and asks for a strict JSON array. The `[[...]]` links it asks for are internal note links, which is the pack's stated purpose. The reviewer persona treats its input as untrusted, rejects by default, enforces the same narrow format and keeps a strict one-sentence JSON reply. There are no templates. Nothing in the files is hidden, encoded or misnamed, and none of the text tries to instruct the pack reviewer or the dreaming model. The fixtures are clearly synthetic: a 'sample service', a transcript flagged `synthetic: true`, and generic note titles. The README accurately describes the inputs, how the pack gets work, its output and its cost. Two small inconsistencies make the pack stricter rather than looser, so neither is a reason to reject. First, the persona's rule against links 'the cited turns do not show' may reject links that only the handoff shows. Second, the prompt excludes frontmatter when checking for an existing link, while the persona rejects a link that is present 'in any form'.
